_doc: Script, voice, music and pacing. 'text' = caption words for the beat; 'tts' = what the voice model reads ('Sirix-DB' so the name is spoken as one word; 'by-temporal' so bitemporal is pronounced right). Used by gen_voice.sh, gen_music.sh, tools/*.py. Changing text/tts only takes effect after ./gen_voice.sh N (costs credits).

voice.delivery: [voice: calm, credible, measured technical narrator; warm, clear, unhurried; starts speaking immediately]

music._slowed: audio/music.m4a is the generated track audio/music.20261115-190734.m4a played 1.1324 times slower (resampled, so about 2 semitones lower) with two repeats so it covers the slower film: its 18.1 s main passage (19.1 s to 37.2 s) plays twice, and one 3.0 s bar (from 43.75 s of the slowed track) plays twice; each join is a 0.3 s crossfade. That puts the track's last chord right after the last spoken word. audio/music.slowed-72s.m4a is the version without repeats. skip_lead_in is how much of the track's start is skipped; a newly generated track needs it set again
music.prompt: Understated modern electronic background music for a calm technical product explainer. Warm analog pads, a soft pulsing synth arpeggio, light restrained percussion, about 92 BPM, steady and confident, no vocals, no big drops, mixes well under a voiceover, ends with a gentle resolved final chord.

timing._pace: tempo 0.9 plays the voice 10% slower (pitch kept); pauses inside a take keep their natural length up to max_pause_in_take. A beat's take_pauses sets single pauses of its take by position (seconds before tempo, null = natural), used on beat 3 so each shell query has time to run.

beats.text: You update a record. The old value is gone.
beats.tts: You update a record. The old value is gone.

beats.text: SirixDB keeps every version. Each commit writes only what changed and shares the rest, so storage grows with the change, not the history.
beats.tts: Sirix-DB keeps every version. Each commit writes only what changed and shares the rest, so storage grows with the change, not the history.

beats.text: Any revision opens directly: by number, by timestamp, or bitemporally. Nothing to replay: revision one reads like the latest.
beats.tts: Any revision opens directly: by number, by timestamp, or by-temporally. Nothing to replay: revision one reads like the latest.

beats.text: Every field keeps its identity across revisions. Follow one value through time, or diff any two revisions: exact inserts, updates and deletes.
beats.tts: Every field keeps its identity across revisions. Follow one value through time, or diff any two revisions: exact inserts, updates and deletes.

beats.text: And it's bitemporal: SirixDB knows when a fact was recorded and when it was true, so a correction never erases what you knew.
beats.tts: And it's bitemporal: Sirix-DB knows when a fact was recorded and when it was true, so a correction never erases what you knew.

beats.text: Its indexes are versioned too, including columnar projections for fast analytics on any revision.
beats.tts: Its indexes are versioned too, including columnar projections for fast analytics on any revision.

beats.text: Embed it as a Java library, run the REST server, use the shell, or let AI agents edit safely over MCP.
beats.tts: Embed it as a Java library, run the REST server, use the shell, or let AI agents edit safely over MCP.

beats.text: SirixDB. Every version of your data, kept and queryable as fast as the present. Append-only, bitemporal, embeddable, and open source.
beats.tts: Sirix-DB. Every version of your data, kept and queryable as fast as the present. Append-only, by-temporal, embeddable, and open source.

That take was generated with one more sentence after 'open source.' ('That is Sirix-DB.', cut off again): this voice whispers or drops the vowel of the very last word of a recording, and of seven takes it is the one where 'source' is fully spoken. 'and' before the last item makes the sentence close on 'open source'.
